uncited: Data augmentation generates diverse training samples from synthetic sensor data to improve the robustness and generalization of neural scene representations.
It addresses the problem of limited or biased training distributions by applying geometric transformations and inserting synthetic objects.

Unlike [Novel View Synthesis Rendering](6402-novel-view-synthesis-rendering.md), which synthesizes new views of existing geometry, or [Sparse View Selection and Dataset Configuration](18846-sparse-view-selection-and-dataset-configuration.md), which selects existing captures, data augmentation actively modifies the input data distribution.
It builds on [Synthetic Dataset Generation](9337-synthetic-dataset-generation.md) by adding stochastic variation to poses, signs, and scene content.
The method consists of two primary strategies: random rotation of existing data and dataset-specific sign balancing.
*   Camera poses $T$ (position and orientation).
*   Sensor measurements $Z_t = \{v_i, r_{t,i}\}$, where $v_i$ is the ray direction and $r_{t,i}$ is the range measurement at sensor position $p_t$ and orientation $R_t$.
*   CAD models (optional, for object insertion).
*   Augmented dataset $D$ containing samples $(p_j, v_j, f^*_j, i^*_j, s^*_j)$.
Generate random rotation angles $\theta_x, \theta_y, \theta_z$.
Construct rotation matrices $R_x(\theta_x)$, $R_y(\theta_y)$, $R_z(\theta_z)$.
Compute total rotation $R_{total} = R_z(\theta_z) R_y(\theta_y) R_x(\theta_x)$.
Apply $R_{total}$ to all points in the point cloud.
Apply $R_{total}$ to the rotation component of all camera poses.
It is chosen when training implicit signed distance functions that require balanced positive and negative samples.
It is chosen when the training data lacks sufficient variety in object types or appearances.
*   **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of samples for rotation and sign balancing.
Object insertion adds rendering overhead proportional to the number of inserted objects.
*   **When to use:** When training data is limited or biased towards specific poses/signs.
Data augmentation in this context originated from the need to train robust neural scene representations from synthetic data.
